title: LottieFiles Web & Marketing
summary: Evolved LottieFiles’ web presence into a more mature, cohesive expression of the brand and its motion-first identity

highlight.title: Raised the standard for design, visuals, and animation across LottieFiles, creating a shared direction that extended beyond the initial web work

description:
I led the design and visual direction for LottieFiles’ web presence, helping shape the wider evolution of the brand and raise the standard for design, visuals, and animation across both marketing and product experiences. I started with the homepage, animation pages, and tools pages, then worked on the Lottie Creator landing page. Across these projects, I shaped the information architecture, UX, UI, interaction design, motion, and reusable structural patterns behind the new visual language.

Once the direction was established, I guided its rollout across the wider marketing site. I worked with other designers as existing pages were migrated and new ones were created, providing guidance to keep the work consistent with the new visual language and system. I led stakeholder reviews, ran regular design reviews, conducted design QA, and gave final design approval before release.

insights.label: Why it mattered
insights.body: As LottieFiles grew, its web presence needed a more mature and cohesive visual direction without losing its playfulness and focus on motion.

insights.label: Key decision
insights.body: Created a shared visual direction and flexible structural, interaction, and motion patterns that could be extended consistently across the site.

insights.label: Outcome
insights.body: The new direction gave other designers a clearer foundation to build from, while stronger review, approval, and QA processes helped maintain consistency and quality as the work expanded.

whatScaled: The visual language, structural patterns, interaction principles, and approach to motion became a reusable system for new and migrated pages, allowing other designers to extend the work consistently.

title: LottieFiles Digital Asset Management
summary: Expanded LottieFiles Platform beyond animation into a workspace for managing and delivering multiple asset formats

highlight.title: Gave teams one place to organize, review, version, and deliver animations alongside images, SVGs, videos, and source files

description:
I led the UX, UI, and product workflows that expanded LottieFiles Platform to support images, SVGs, videos, and source files alongside animations. Early in the project, I built an AI-assisted proof of concept to make the core model and workflows tangible, helping stakeholders, product, and engineering align before moving into high-fidelity design.

Rather than creating a separate destination, I extended the existing asset model so these formats could use the organization, status, review, approval, versioning, and delivery workflows teams already knew. I also improved everyday asset management with multi-format and folder uploads, multi-file copy-and-paste, and drag-and-drop organization.

I defined the core Platform experience, guided how the model extended into the plugins, and designed the corresponding Lottie Creator experience, where I also contributed to front-end implementation.

insights.label: Why it mattered
insights.body: Customer requests and our own internal workflows highlighted a broader problem: related project assets were being managed across multiple services, making complete projects harder to organize, track, and deliver.

insights.label: Key decision
insights.body: Built on the existing asset model instead of creating a separate product area, preserving familiar workflows while adapting previews, metadata, and actions to the needs of each format.

insights.label: Outcome
insights.body: Teams adopted the experience to bring related project assets into one workspace, while stable CDN links and version control allowed deployed assets to be updated without redeploying products.

whatScaled: The expanded asset model became shared infrastructure across Platform, Creator, and plugins, supporting consistent asset management and delivery across surfaces and later projects like Motion Systems.

title: LottieFiles Motion Systems
summary: Created a central place for teams to define, manage, publish, and version their motion standards

highlight.title: Established a governed motion system across Platform, Creator, Figma, and After Effects, bringing motion standards into the tools where teams work

description:
Building on an initial proof of concept, I led the UX and UI for Motion Systems within LottieFiles Platform. I developed the end-to-end experience, from setup and brand guide import to managing principles, tokens, easing curves, presets, and approved assets, with support for drafting, publishing, and versioning systems. The initial values and structure were shaped with LottieFiles’ internal Motion Design team to keep the system useful without becoming overly complex. I also contributed directly to front-end implementation within Platform.

Platform served as the source of truth, while Lottie Creator and the Figma and After Effects plugins consumed published standards and made approved tokens, easing curves, presets, and assets available where teams created motion.

I set the direction for Motion Systems in Lottie Creator, working closely with the Creator designer and engineers to translate the Platform model into the creation workflow. I also reviewed the Figma and After Effects plugin experiences, providing feedback to keep their implementations aligned with the core model. Throughout the coordinated release, I conducted design QA to maintain consistency and quality through implementation. The release also received positive feedback from external users.

insights.label: Why it mattered
insights.body: Teams were managing motion standards through incomplete or disconnected systems, leaving them without a reliable way to define, govern, and reuse motion consistently.

insights.label: Key decision
insights.body: Created one consistent structure for building and governing Motion Systems in Platform, then extended published standards into Creator and the plugins.

insights.label: Outcome
insights.body: Motion Systems launched as a coordinated experience across Platform, Creator, Figma, and After Effects, giving teams a consistent way to define, publish, and reuse motion standards.

whatScaled: The model established in Platform became the foundation for governing Motion Systems across the wider LottieFiles ecosystem, giving teams a consistent way to apply standards across creative workflows. It also helped kickstart broader governance initiatives within the Platform team.

title: LottieFiles Developer Handoff
summary: Turned fragmented implementation guidance into a context-aware handoff tailored to each developer’s stack

highlight.title: Brought asset details, technical requirements, setup guidance, and ready-to-use code into one focused implementation workflow

stats.label: from early concept to production experience
phased rollout to validate implementation friction

description:
Customer feedback and product data showed that developers, particularly those implementing Lottie for the first time, struggled to turn animation assets into production-ready implementations. Technical details, requirements, and setup guidance were spread across several places, creating friction between receiving an asset and shipping it.

The project began as an early idea rather than a defined solution. I worked directly with the Head of Product to clarify the problem, explore possible directions, and shape the concept. I built an AI-assisted proof of concept for a focused, full-page handoff experience, using it to align the team before developing the direction into high-fidelity design.

I designed the handoff as a context-aware workflow that brought asset details, technical specifications, setup instructions, and ready-to-use code into one workspace, adapting the guidance to the developer’s selected platform, framework, player, and animation features. I owned the UX and UI, worked closely with Engineering throughout implementation, and conducted design QA before rollout.

insights.label: Why it mattered
insights.body: Developers needed a clearer path from receiving an animation to implementing it correctly. Generic documentation still left them to interpret asset requirements and determine which instructions applied to their stack.

insights.label: Key decision
insights.body: Instead of sending developers to generic documentation, I designed a dynamic integration guide that adapted setup steps and code to the selected platform, framework, player, and animation features.

insights.label: Outcome
insights.body: The experience entered a phased A/B rollout with a small group of users, allowing the team to validate whether the new handoff flow reduced implementation friction before expanding availability.

whatScaled: The dynamic guide established a reusable structure for tailoring implementation support across platforms, frameworks, players, and animation features. New development stacks could be added without creating a separate handoff flow for each setup.

title: Lummi Figma plugin

solution: I brought discovery and insertion into one focused plugin, letting designers search, browse, and place single or multiple images without leaving Figma. Shared patterns kept the experience familiar to existing Lummi users.

title: Musho Figma Plugin
summary: Reimagined AI page creation as a conversation
description: Designed components and product views for the Musho Figma plugin, including an exploration of a chat-based AI workflow. The concept replaced a sequence of isolated actions with a more conversational experience for generating and refining landing-page content.
problem: The existing action-based workflow asked designers to break creative intent into a sequence of isolated commands. Generating and refining a page felt fragmented because each step provided limited context for the larger idea.
solution: I explored a conversational workflow that carried context between prompts. Designers could describe an idea, review the result, and refine the page through one continuous exchange inside Figma.

title: Buenoverse
summary: Made choosing an avatar feel like part of the adventure
description: Designed the avatar-selection interface for Buenoverse, balancing creative flexibility with a clear and approachable experience. The work focused on navigation, customization, visual feedback, and a cohesive presentation that helped players choose how they entered the world.
problem: The first step into Buenoverse involved a wide range of avatar choices and customization options. Too much complexity risked turning an exciting opening moment into a setup task.
solution: I shaped a visually led selection flow with clear navigation and immediate feedback. Players could explore their options confidently while the interface preserved the playful character of the world they were about to enter.

title: Bueno Drops Figma Plugin
summary: Turned Figma artwork into launch-ready digital collectibles
description: Led the design of the Bueno Drops Figma Plugin, creating a focused workflow that helped artists turn designs into digital collectibles without coding. I streamlined the flow, designed an accessible interface, and supported both Open and Limited Edition drops from setup through launch.
problem: Artists could create their work in Figma, but publishing it as a digital collectible required technical knowledge and a chain of unfamiliar tools. That gap added friction between creation and launch, especially for less technical creators.
solution: I designed an end-to-end plugin flow that guided artists from selected artwork through edition type, configuration, and launch. A few clear steps reduced the technical burden while preserving control over the final drop.
